small_guidance:
- The kernel computes a 4×4×4 output tile per program with deeply nested static loops over (4·4·4)·KD·KH·KW·IC iterations — too much per program. Shrink to a 2×2×2 or 1×1×1 spatial tile per program to expose more parallelism, and increase `num_warps` to 4 so each program has more threads to hide memory latency.
- Wrap the kernel in `@triton.autotune` over `BLOCK_OC ∈ {16, 32}`, spatial tile size ∈ {1, 2, 4}, `num_warps ∈ {2, 4, 8}`, `num_stages ∈ {2, 3}` keyed on `(OC, PD_OD*PD_OH*PD_OW)`.
- Hoist the weight load out of the spatial tile loop: weights `w[ic, oc, kd, kh, kw]` are reused across all 64 voxels in the current tile — load them once into registers/SMEM before the spatial sub-loops instead of reloading per voxel.
large_guidance:
- Restructure as a gather-GEMM in im2col form: one program per `(N, pooled-spatial tile, OC tile)`, with a K-loop over `IC*KD*KH*KW` doing `tl.dot` of a tile of im2col-gathered input columns against a weight tile. The current scalar-per-(ic) inner loop wastes the tensor cores; using `tl.dot` on `[BM, BK] x [BK, BN]` with BM=output-tile×pool-window, BN=OC, BK=IC*KH*KW chunks will give 10-30× more throughput.
- Fold the two 2×2×2 avg-pools (= one 4×4×4 mean) into the epilogue by accumulating into a single pooled accumulator across the 64 sub-voxels — but compute each sub-voxel via GEMM rather than scalar MACs. Output one pooled value per `(n, oc, pd, ph, pw)`; the kernel writes `N*OC*PD_OD*PD_OH*PD_OW` elements total.
- Switch layout to NDHWC (channels_last) so the OC axis (the GEMM-N) and IC axis (part of GEMM-K) are contiguous in memory, allowing coalesced vector loads of weight rows and input columns.
